summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with confusion and groin pain, found to be due to a urinary tract infection caused by multidrug-resistant E. coli, in the setting of a chronic indwelling Foley catheter. He was started on IV cefepime, which improved his mental status, tremors, and overall condition. He developed transient anisocoria, likely due to anticholinergic medication, which resolved after discontinuation. Volume overload contributed to hypoxia and pleural effusions, managed with Lasix and diuresis. His infection resolved, and he was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with plans to restart Macrobid prophylaxis, manage constipation, and follow up with urology.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Infection with microorganisms with resistance to multiple drugs
